sop-from-memo.output:
Water Heater Replacement

You will need: water shut-off wrench, breaker panel access, garden hose, drain into floor drain, new flex lines (always new), expansion tank check, camera for file photo.

Steps

1. Shut the water at the main valve (do not rely on the small isolation valve). Turn off the breaker serving the water heater.

2. Connect the garden hose from the van to the drain outlet and run it to the floor drain. Open the drain valve and let the tank empty completely.

3. Disconnect the incoming and outgoing water lines from the old tank.

4. Remove the old water heater and position the new one in place.

5. Connect new flex lines to both water inlet and outlet (use new lines every time, even if old ones appear intact).

6. Fill the tank by opening the main water valve. Leave the breaker off.

7. Bleed air from the system by opening the faucet closest to the water heater until water runs clear.

8. Switch the breaker back on once bleeding is complete.

9. Wait 20 minutes, then inspect all connections and joints for leaks.

10. Take a photograph of the installed unit and place it in the job file.

Done looks like: Tank is full, no water dripping from any connection after 20 minutes, air is bled from lines, breaker is on, photo is filed.

Common mistakes

1. Powering up before the air is bled. Check: water comes out smoothly from the test faucet, no sputtering.

2. Not checking for an expansion tank when a check valve sits on the main line. Check: ask the homeowner if the system has a check valve, and if so, verify the expansion tank is present and functioning (ASK OWNER on how to test this if you are unsure).

3. Waiting only 2 minutes for leaks instead of 20. Check: set a timer on your phone for 20 minutes and do not leave the job site until it sounds.
sop-from-memo.spoken: Water heater swap has three critical steps: shut water and breaker first, always install new flex lines, bleed air at the closest faucet before power. Check for leaks after a full 20 minutes, not two. If there is a check valve on the main, confirm the expansion tank is there. Say read the rest to hear everything else.

WHAT TO ASK EACH VENDOR

RECOMMENDATION

Pick Vendor 3 if you commit to 36 months. Lowest total cost ($35,060) and maintenance is included. Condition: Vendor 3's early-exit option at month 12 is a safety valve — but if you think you will use it, the math flips; ask Vendor 3 for the exit cost first.

Avoid Vendor 2 unless maintenance is cheaper than stated — at $95/mo plus overage, it adds up fast.
